Strict version that only accepts real month and day ranges:

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}` is the year, e.g. `2026`
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` is the month, `01` to `12`
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` is the day, `01` to `31`
- `^` and `$` anchor the match to the whole string. Remove them, or use `\b`, to find dates inside longer text.

It matches `2026-10-01` and rejects `2026-13-01`, `2026-10-32` and `2026-1-1`.

The regex can't tell how many days each month has, so it still accepts dates like `2026-02-30`. If you need to rule those out, check the value with a date parser after the regex matches. For example, in Python: `datetime.date.fromisoformat(s)`.

If you only need the shape and don't care whether the month and day are in range, this is enough: `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`
